truthAudit.Summary: Run 1 found 12 truth items fully, 2 partially, and missed 6. Several found items had severity or CWE misclassifications, and at least one finding (admin exec) was not supported by the provided true vulnerability set.

Items.Notes: The audited answer quoted runtime_log_format() and printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input), matching the true format-string injection, but rated it High instead of Critical.
The audited answer contains no finding about the fact() lambda's result *= i integer overflow.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free when memory pool is cleaned while thread-pool tasks still run
Items.Notes: It identifies stage_deferred_history_flush enqueuing delayed scratch reads, followed by memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup, matching the true use-after-free.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection in validate_config using system()
Items.Notes: It identifies validator_path/config_file concatenation passed to system(), matching the true config validation command injection, but rated High instead of Critical.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded strcpy into input_buffer_ due to inverted length check
Items.Notes: The audited answer found the strcpy(input_buffer_) path and separately noted the safe_string_copy terminator off-by-one, but it split the input-processing stack buffer overflow into separate findings and overclaimed the main finding's severity as Critical versus High.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: ThreadSafeCounter increment reads value before locking
Items.Notes: It identifies old_value being read before lock_guard and then written, matching the thread-pool counter race, but rated Low instead of Medium.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Authentication bypass via EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE after five attempts
Items.Notes: It identifies login_attempts_ > 5, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, and authenticated_ = true, matching the logic bomb, but classified it as CWE-287 rather than CWE-511.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Path traversal in ConfigLoader::load_config via admin load
Items.Notes: It identifies config_dir_ + filename in load_config and admin load reachability, matching the true path traversal.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded strcpy into fixed 256-byte expression buffer in parser
Items.Notes: It identifies buffer_size_ = 256 and strcpy(expression_buffer_, expr_str.c_str()) in parser::ExpressionParser::parse, matching the heap overflow, but used generic CWE-787 instead of CWE-122.
It identifies ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH, matching the hardcoded administrator credentials, but rated Critical instead of High.
It identifies std::mt19937, uniform_int_distribution, and 1000, 9999 for session tokens, matching the weak PRNG/session-token weakness, but used CWE-330 and Medium instead of CWE-338 and High.
The audited answer contains no finding about the static std::tm cached_time/localtime data race in logging.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Shell command injection through TEMP/TMPDIR in append_override_audit_event
Items.Notes: It identified the TEMP/TMPDIR/supercalc_emergency.log/system code, but framed it primarily as command injection rather than the true insecure temporary file handling item.
No previous finding addresses persistent authenticated_ state, login_attempts_, or session_token_ as a session-persistence weakness.
No previous finding addresses unhandled std::stod(tokens[3]) in handle_variable_command.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Size_t underflow in MemoryPool block split can create out-of-bounds fragment
Items.Notes: It identifies previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES and fragment.size = remaining, matching the integer underflow, but rated High instead of Critical.
No previous finding addresses unbounded recursion through parse_expression/parse_factor/PAREN_OPEN.
It identifies evaluate_cached mutating result_cache_ without cache_mutex_ and reachability via thread_pool_->enqueue, matching the data race.
No previous finding addresses the std::filesystem::exists / sleep_for / std::ifstream TOCTOU in config loading.
It identifies token_length and 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length), matching the division-by-zero, but rated Medium instead of Low.
